primary_question: Does controlled separation + retention produce a reproducible, clinically meaningful exposure advantage over CereVasc's existing platform without compromising drainage?
comparator: CereVasc US11850390B2 (existing endovascular delivery — NOT lumbar puncture)
commercial_context: CereVasc has demonstrated ovine CNS biodistribution via eShunt and is seeking pharma partners. This experiment directly tests whether the architecture increases the value of that platform.

design.group_A: CereVasc baseline (endovascular delivery, no separation, no retention)
design.agent: FITC-dextran 150 kDa (primary) + scAAV9 (secondary, CereVasc has biodistribution data)
design.sampling: Tissue: post-mortem fluorescence; CSF: 0,0.5,1,2,4,8,12,24,48h; Venous: same; ICP: continuous; Drainage: continuous

endpoints.primary: Target-tissue AUC (brain-adjacent tissue drug concentration × time)
endpoints.therapeutic_relevance: For FITC-dextran: PK proxy (no PD target). For scAAV9: transduction efficiency (CereVasc has published data for comparison).

decision_tree.AUC_B >= 200% AUC_A AND drainage safe: BUYABLE CONFIRMED — controlled exposure advantage demonstrated
decision_tree.AUC_B 120-200% AUC_A AND drainage safe: MILESTONE-WORTHY — advantage confirmed, magnitude smaller; recalibrate model
decision_tree.AUC_B <= 120% AUC_A: TRUE CEILING — model overestimated in vivo
